arxiv-2301-05187.title: WIRE: Wavelet Implicit Neural Representations
arxiv-2301-05187.creator: Vishwanath Saragadam, Daniel LeJeune, Jasper Tan, Guha Balakrishnan
arxiv-2301-05187.description: Abstract Implicit neural representations (INRs) have recently advanced numerous vision-related areas. INR performance depends strongly on the choice of the nonlinear activation function employed in its multilayer perceptron (MLP) network. A wide range of nonlinearities have been explored, but, unfortunately, current INRs designed to have high accuracy also suffer from poor robustness (to signal noise, parameter variation, etc.).

arxiv-2401-14982.title: Minimum-dissipation principle for synchronised stochastic oscillators far from equilibrium
arxiv-2401-14982.creator: Jan Meibohm, Massimiliano Esposito
arxiv-2401-14982.description: Abstract We prove a linear stability-dissipation relation (SDR) for q q -state Potts models driven far from equilibrium by a nonconservative force. At a critical coupling strength, these models exhibit a synchronisation transition from a decoherent into a synchronised state.

arxiv-2402-17412.title: DiffuseKronA: A Parameter Efficient Fine-tuning Method for Personalized Diffusion Models
arxiv-2402-17412.creator: Shyam Marjit, Harshit Singh, Nityanand Mathur, Sayak Paul, Chia-Mu Yu, Pin-Yu Chen
arxiv-2402-17412.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shyam Marjit, Harshit Singh, Nityanand Mathur, Sayak Paul, Chia-Mu Yu, Pin-Yu Chen. In the realm of subject-driven text-to-image (T2I) generative models, recent developments like DreamBooth and BLIP-Diffusion have led to impressive results yet encounter limitations due to their intensive fine-tuning demands and substantial parameter requirements. While the low-rank adaptation (LoRA) module within DreamBooth offers a reduction in trainable parameters, it introduces a pronounced sensitivity to hyperparameters, leading to a compromise between parameter efficiency and the quality of T2I personalized image synthesis.

arxiv-2404-02218.title: A shared compilation stack for distributed-memory parallelism in stencil DSLs Conference: 29th ACM International Conference on Architectural Support for Programming Languages and Operating Systems, Volume 3; April 27-May 1, 2024; La Jolla, CA, USA 29th ACM International Conference on Architectural S
arxiv-2404-02218.creator: George Bisbas, Anton Lydike, Emilien Bauer, Nick Brown, Mathieu Fehr, Lawrence Mitchell, Gabriel Rodriguez-Canal, Maurice Jamieson, Paul H. J. Kelly, Michel Steuwer, Tobias Grosser
arxiv-2404-02218.description: Abstract . Domain Specific Languages (DSLs) increase programmer productivity and provide high performance. Their targeted abstractions allow scientists to express problems at a high level, providing rich details that optimizing compilers can exploit to target current- and next-generation supercomputers. The convenience and performance of DSLs come with significant development and maintenance costs.

arxiv-2408-04195.title: Design and Implementation of Smart Infrastructures and Connected Vehicles in A Mini-city Platform
arxiv-2408-04195.creator: Daniel Vargas, Ethan Haque, Matthew Carroll, Daniel Perez, Tyler Roman, Phong Nguyen, Golnaz Habibi
arxiv-2408-04195.description: Abstract This paper presents a 1/10th scale mini-city platform used as a testing bed for evaluating autonomous and connected vehicles. Using the mini-city platform, we can evaluate different driving scenarios including human-driven and autonomous driving. We provide a unique, visual feature-rich environment for evaluating computer vision methods.

arxiv-2507-20999.title: LoRA-PAR: A Flexible Dual-System LoRA Partitioning Approach to Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning
arxiv-2507-20999.creator: Yining Huang, Bin Li, Keke Tang, Meilian Chen
arxiv-2507-20999.description: Abstract Large-scale generative models like DeepSeek-R1 and OpenAI-O1 benefit substantially from chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, yet pushing their performance typically requires vast data, large model sizes, and full-parameter fine-tuning. While parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) helps reduce cost, most existing approaches primarily address domain adaptation or layer-wise allocation rather than explicitly tailoring data and parameters to different response demands.

arxiv-2509-14712.title: From Ground Trust † to Truth: Disparities in Offensive Language Judgments on Contemporary Korean Political Discourse
arxiv-2509-14712.creator: Seunguk Yu, Jungmin Yun, Jinhee Jang, Youngbin Kim
arxiv-2509-14712.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Seunguk Yu, Jungmin Yun, Jinhee Jang, Youngbin Kim. Warning: this paper contains expressions that may offend the readers. Although offensive language continually evolves over time, even recent studies using LLMs have predominantly relied on outdated datasets and rarely evaluated the generalization ability on unseen texts. In this study, we constructed a large-scale dataset of contemporary political discourse and employed three refined judgments in the absence of ground truth. Each judgment reflects a representative offensive language detection method and is carefully designed for optimal conditions.

arxiv-2510-26988.title: Inferring the Chemotaxis Distortion Function from Cellular Decision Strategies
arxiv-2510-26988.creator: Fardad Vakilipoor, Johannes Konrad, Maximilian Schäfer
arxiv-2510-26988.description: Abstract Cellular intelligence enables cells to process environmental signals and make context-dependent decisions, as exemplified by chemotaxis, where cells navigate chemical gradients despite noisy signaling pathways. To investigate how cells deal with uncertainty, we apply an information-theoretic framework based on RDT ( RDT ).

arxiv-2511-15499.title: Learning to Expand Images for Efficient Visual Autoregressive Modeling
arxiv-2511-15499.creator: Ruiqing Yang, Kaixin Zhang, Zheng Zhang, Shan You, Tao Huang
arxiv-2511-15499.description: Abstract Autoregressive models have recently shown great promise in visual generation by leveraging discrete token sequences akin to language modeling. However, existing approaches often suffer from inefficiency, either due to token-by-token decoding or the complexity of multi-scale representations. In this work, we introduce Expanding Autoregressive Representation (EAR), a novel generation paradigm that emulates the human visual system’s center-outward perception pattern.

pmc-10641899.title: Identification of HuR–RNA Interfering Compounds by Dynamic Combinatorial Chemistry and Fluorescence Polarization
pmc-10641899.creator: Serena
pmc-10641899.description: The RNA binding protein HuR regulates the post-transcriptional process of different oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes, and its dysregulation is linked with cancer. Thus, modulating the complex HuR–RNA represents a promising anticancer strategy. To search for novel HuR ligands able to interfere with the HuR–RNA complex, the protein-templated dynamic combinatorial chemistry (pt-DCC) method was utilized.

pmc-10671377.title: The Relative Burden of Occupational Injuries and Illnesses in Firefighters: An Analysis of Washington Workers’ Compensation Claims, 2006–2020
pmc-10671377.creator: Naomi Anderson, Jennifer Marcum, David Bonauto, Miriam Siegel, Claire LaSee
pmc-10671377.description: Firefighters face many hazards on the job and have a high rate of work-related injuries and illnesses (WRII). We analyzed Washington workers’ compensation claims from 2006–2020 to characterize WRII in firefighters compared to law enforcement officers and “all other” workers. There were 9187 compensable claims for firefighters, 7801 for law enforcement officers, and 586,939 for “all other” workers.

pmc-11603830.title: Partnering RemoTe monitoring of Implanted Cardiac devices with Intelligent PATient Engagement – PARTICIPATE trial: a protocol for a randomised controlled trial
pmc-11603830.creator: Brodie Sheahen, Liliana Laranjo, Gopal Sivagangabalan, Tim Shaw, Aravinda Thiagalingam, Clara K Chow
pmc-11603830.description: IntroductionCardiac implantable electronic devices (CIED) can transfer data to the healthcare team, remotely. National and international cardiac organisations recommend all patients use this technology, however patient engagement is suboptimal. Previously, in cardiovascular patients, SMS messaging services have shown improvements in patient engagement and subsequent health outcomes.

pmc-11608484.title: Quality of life and caregiving burden associated with parenting a person with Duchenne/Becker muscular dystrophy in Poland
pmc-11608484.creator: Jan Domaradzki, Dariusz Walkowiak
pmc-11608484.description: BackgroundDuchenne and Becker muscular dystrophies (DBMD) are rare progressive, X-linked diseases of muscle wasting characterised by the early onset and prognosis of premature death. The aim of this study was to evaluate the impact of providing care for a person with DBMD on caregivers’ quality of life, perceived burden and financial well-being.

pmc-11679844.title: Functional Rehabilitation in Non-Reconstructed Hemimandibulectomy Patients
pmc-11679844.creator: Edoardo Brauner, Federico Laudoni, Emilia Rampelli, Andrea Bellizzi, Francesca De Angelis, Nicola Pranno, Andrea Battisti, Valentino Valentini, Stefano Di Carlo
pmc-11679844.description: Background and Objectives: Functional rehabilitation in patients with hemimandibulectomy remains a challenge no matter what method of reconstruction is chosen by physicians. In this paper, we aim to evaluate the feasibility of an acceptable occlusal restoration in patients who have undergone hemimanidublectomy without the reestablishment of mandibular continuity.

pmc-12470271.title: Age-Related Patterns in Pediatric Road Traffic Injuries in Romania
pmc-12470271.creator: Ștefan Popa, Carmen Iulia Ciongradi, Adrian Onisim Surd, Ioan Sârbu, Iuliana-Laura Candussi, Irene Paula Popa
pmc-12470271.description: Background: Pediatric road traffic injuries (RTIs) represent a significant public health concern, particularly in countries like Romania, where road infrastructure and safety remain challenges. Despite recent economic reclassification, Romania continues to report high rates of pediatric traffic-related injuries. Non-fatal RTIs often result in long-term physical and psychological harm.

pmc-12681826.title: Identification of novel Menin-MLL interaction inhibitors targeting leukemia using in-silico virtual screening and structure-based drug design approaches
pmc-12681826.creator: Amany I Almars, Shahad W Kattan
pmc-12681826.description: Leukemogenesis fundamentally depends on the interaction between Menin and MLL1 fusion proteins, especially in the context of aggressive mixed-lineage leukemia (MLL)-rearranged subtypes. This interaction can be disrupted to facilitate a focused therapeutic strategy. This study aimed to employ a comprehensive in silico drug repurposing strategy to identify new inhibitors of the Menin-MLL1 interaction.

pmc-13152927.title: Morphological description of the tongue of the Boa constrictor
pmc-13152927.creator: Thamara Cozzi Gonçalves, Isabella Bittencourt Pires Chaves, Rogério Antonio Ribeiro Rodrigues, Elane Guerreiro Giese, Érika Branco, Ana Rita de Lima
pmc-13152927.description: The Amazon biome hosts a rich diversity of reptile species, including Boa constrictor (Linnaeus, 1758), widely distributed throughout Brazil and belonging to the order Squamata. Despite its ecological importance, detailed descriptions of lingual morphology in this species remain limited. This study aimed to describe the tongue of B. constrictor using macroscopic, histological, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analyses.

pmc-13317913.title: Clinical Competence of Neuroscience Nurses in Inpatient Wards and Intensive Care Units: A Mixed-Methods Systematic Review
pmc-13317913.creator: Inkeri Hutri, Tiia Saastamoinen, Aki Laakso, Toni Haapa
pmc-13317913.description: BACKGROUND:Neuroscience nurses need clinical competence (CC) when taking care of neuropatients. In this study the selected nursing context is inpatient wards and intensive care units (ICU) in university hospitals and tertiary referral centers where neuroscience patients are treated 24/7, patients’ conditions can change rapidly, and nurses execute clinical interventions continually for adult patients.

pmc-4053813.creator: Derrick E Wood, Steven L Salzberg
pmc-4053813.description: Peer-reviewed research article (PubMed Central). Kraken is an ultrafast and highly accurate program for assigning taxonomic labels to metagenomic DNA sequences.
